religion-language-diffusion-tree.alt: Tree diagram of part of the Indo-European language family. Four branches: Germanic (English, German, Dutch, Swedish), Romance (Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian), Slavic (Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, Czech) and Indo-Iranian (Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, Persian). A note says the order is family, then branch, then language, that dialects are versions of one language, and that only some branches are shown.

religion-language-diffusion-spread.alt: Two panels. Universalizing religions: arrows go out in every direction from the hearth; they seek new followers anywhere and spread by expansion and relocation diffusion; examples Christianity, Islam, Buddhism and Sikhism. Ethnic religions: most followers stay in a ring near the hearth, and one dashed arrow shows relocation when followers migrate; examples Hinduism and Judaism.
